lessons: Central positions generally enhance pick success but blocks moved too close to central x-values may still fail.
Successful placements require avoiding extreme y-values except in zone_C where reliability is higher; repositioning blocks towards moderate y values helps in other zones.
Blocks around x = -9 to +8 with moderate y values are reliably pickable and placeable, but placement can succeed even if moved further from initial position or pushed closer to central coordinates.
Placements in zone_C can be successful even with extreme y-values; picks from extreme positions often fail unless block is near-central without being overly adjusted towards center.
Pushing blocks too close to the exact center from an already moderate position may cause pick failure, indicating a sweet spot exists beyond merely central x-values.

Blocks at (-3.2, +0.6) and similar moderate y values demonstrate reliable picks and placements when moderately adjusted towards central coordinates without being overly centered; avoid extreme y-values for successful placement.
